title: Adaptive streaming backpressure and result adapter for chained tool pipelines
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: When composing multiple tool/function calls in a single request, we need (1) a streaming-safe execution loop that supports partial/tool-level backpressure, (2) adapters that map heterogeneous tool outputs into a canonical structured-output schema, and (3) robust recursion/loop detection so chains cannot spin indefinitely or create exponential fanout. Current runtime either executes tools synchronously (blocking) or streams raw tool output without schema guarantees, which leads to latency spikes, unbounded memory growth, and downstream parsing failures for structured consumers.

Goal: Implement an adaptive result-adapter and flow-control layer in the tool execution loop that can: (A) negotiate streaming capability per-tool at start-of-invocation, (B) apply chunk-level backpressure and buffer windows to preserve tail latency SLOs, (C) normalize tool outputs into the platform structured-output contract (with validation and forgiving transforms), and (D) detect and short-circuit recursion loops or runaway cyclic chains with configurable policies. The feature must be backwards-compatible with existing non-streaming tools and provide an opt-in strict mode for schema enforcement.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end multi-tool YAML/JSON structured output normalization verified in CI for 5 sample tool-chains (PR integration tests)
Streaming chains respect per-request latency SLO: p95 tail latency increase < 10% compared to blocking baseline for 95% of synthetic workloads
Backpressure mechanism prevents memory growth for high-rate generators (no OOM in stress test with 200 concurrent chains)
Recursion guard halts chains exceeding configured call-graph depth or repeated tool signatures and returns a well-formed error payload
Rollout toggle via config flag and metrics: runtime-1.19 ships feature off by default and on for internal canary account
design_decisions: Two-mode execution adapter: permissive-streaming (default) that accepts looser schemas and performs streaming normalization, and strict-schema mode that enforces types and rejects/rolls back if normalization fails.

Backpressure model: credit-based window per tool (configurable window size) implemented at stream-chunk boundaries. Upstream producers yield when their outgoing credits are exhausted; adapter buffers up to window and applies eviction/compaction policy.

Compatibility layer: at invocation handshake, runtime queries tool metadata (supports_streaming: boolean, output_schema_versions: list). If tool doesn't support streaming, runtime transparently runs it in a blocking adapter that emits a single structured message to downstream consumers.

Recursion detection: maintain lightweight call-signature fingerprint (tool_key + input-hash truncated) with TTL and max-repeat threshold. If repeated signature observed beyond threshold within TTL, short-circuit and return error with trace IDs for debugging.
KV-cache interactions: streaming adapters checkpoint partial KV writes only at safe commit boundaries to avoid divergent KV states when a chain is aborted mid-stream.
Telemetry: emit per-chain metrics (streamed_bytes, buffered_bytes, backpressure_events, recursion_hits, normalization_errors) and tracing spans for each adapter boundary.
tradeoffs: Permissive streaming increases availability but can mask schema regressions; strict mode increases safety but could break integrations if schemas evolve without coordination.
Credit-based backpressure adds protocol complexity (bookkeeping) but yields predictable memory bounds compared to naive buffering.
Call-signature TTLs may under-detect long-running legitimate loops; chosen thresholds bias toward safety to prevent customer impact.
Checkpointing KV only at commit boundaries reduces risk of inconsistent state but may increase re-computation cost on retries.

test_plan: Unit: adapter credit accounting, buffer eviction, schema transforms (100% coverage for adapter module)
Integration: compose 5 canonical tool-chains mixing streaming/non-streaming tools and validate final structured output against golden fixtures
Stress: 200 concurrent chains with synthetic generator tools; assert no OOM and p95 latency SLOs
Chaos: inject tool failure mid-stream to validate checkpoint rollback and clear error payloads
rollout_plan: Stage 1 - internal canary: enable for 'internal' org in runtime-1.19 canary cluster for 48h; monitor metrics
Stage 2 - limited beta: enable for selected customers (3 accounts) and run QA scenarios for 7 days
Stage 3 - gradual ramp: 10%->50%->100% across hosted region over 2 weeks with automated rollback on recursion_hits > 0.1%
Rollback: revert flag; run cleanup job to flush partial buffers and reset transient KV checkpoints
monitoring: Metrics to add: runtime.adapter.buffered_bytes, runtime.adapter.backpressure.count, runtime.adapter.recursion.hits, runtime.adapter.normalization.errors
Dashboards: per-route stream health (buffer growth, backpressure rate, normalization error rate)
Alerts: alert if average buffered_bytes > 50MB per node or if recursion_hits spike above configured threshold
notes: Follow-up: add SDK helper that surfaces adapter capability to developers (client-side negotiation) so clients can avoid sending large streaming payloads to non-streaming tools.
Implementation detail: ensure adapter codepath is inlined and optimized – microbench before merging to ensure < 4% p95 overhead for cold-start chains.
